newsitem.title: UK: UK's SIB to extend cooling off to OEIC funds.
newsitem.headline: UK's SIB to extend cooling off to OEIC funds.

text.p: Britain's Securities and Investments Board (SIB) said on Monday that investors in Open Ended Investment Companies (OEICs) will be able to change their minds after making their investment.

It said it would propose to extend cooling off rights to OEICs, giving them the same rights as investors in unit trusts and linked Personal Equity Plans (PEPs) where cooling off regulations will remain unchanged.
The decision follows a six month review of costs and benefits related to cooling off.
The review found that few investors in unit trusts and unit trust PEPs exercise their cooling off rights, but that it did offer benefits for investors at a modest cost.
The SIB said the cost savings from abolishing cooling off would not be sufficient to warrant removal of this safeguard.
OEICs are a collective investment vehicle which can be marketed from Britain into Europe under the 1985 UCITS directive, which allows for cross-border operation of such funds.
The SIB does not expect to authorise the first OEIC to be offered to the market until the summer amid ongoing discussion with tax authorities.

OEICs are closely modelled on UK unit trusts, but have some critical differences. They will offer a single mid-market price rather than a bid-offer spread, and a corporate structure will allow them to borrow.
The SIB also said it was proposing to make the way investors are informed of their cooling off rights less prescriptive and more cost effective.
There are two types of cooling off for non-life products. Cancellation gives investors a right lasting for 14 days to cancel an investment contract once it has been made.
Delayed entry provides that investors' applications to enter into a unit trust PEP are not accepted for a specified period before the contract is made.

Non-life products covered by the announcement include authorised unit trust schemes, recognised collective investment schemes, UK OEICs, PEPs linked to any of the above. Investment trust savings schemes do not attract cooling off rights.
